extracted.intended_audience: aspiring fiction writers / creative-writing students (Gotham Writers' Workshop audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for writing short fiction, covering craft elements (character, dialogue, description, plot) and the business/production side (agents, publishers, submissions). Intended to help writers produce and revise stories for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beginning plot with action
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use action to start the plot—open scenes with movement or event that propels the story rather than static exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking dialogue with action
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine spoken lines with character actions to create momentum and reveal character; avoid dialogue that floats without physical grounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions of characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Character actions should be purposeful and reflect goals, traits, and conflict; use actions to show rather than tell inner states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjectives
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose adjectives judiciously—prefer specific, evocative modifiers and avoid piling on weak or generic adjectives that dull prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advances (publishing advances)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the business-of-writing considerations; understand typical advance expectations and how they fit into contracts and the book-deal process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverbs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use adverbs sparingly; rely on strong verbs and concrete detail instead of adverbs that tell rather than show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agents (finding, role, submission, nonlegitimate agents)
rubrics_metrics.description: agents: finding, nonlegitimate, role of, submitting to
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know how to find legitimate agents, recognize nonlegitimate agents/scams, understand an agent's role, and follow proper submission protocols when seeking representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alliteration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use alliteration as a stylistic device with awareness—can add musicality but avoid distracting or forced repetition of initial sounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antagonist
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop an antagonist with clear motives and presence; the antagonist should generate meaningful conflict for the protagonist rather than existing as a cardboard obstacle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appearance of characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select physical details that are relevant and revealing; avoid laundry-list descriptions—use appearance to illuminate character or situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attributions / tags
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dialogue tags (he said, she asked) appropriately—prefer simple tags and action beats over elaborate or intrusive attributions that call attention to themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards / competitions / grants
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider competitions and grants as part of a writer's career strategy; know submission requirements and what judges typically reward (craft, originality, voice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Book publishers (business of writing)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand publisher roles in acquiring, producing, and marketing books; consider traditional vs. self-publishing when planning a project's path to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business of writing (overall)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers practical industry knowledge: advances, agents, contracts, publicity, money, prepublication, submissions, and what happens after a book deal; plan both craft and career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business: after the book deal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know the post-acquisition processes: editing, production schedules, publicity, and contractual obligations to make the most of a deal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magazine submissions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow each magazine's guidelines, tailor submissions, and understand slush-pile realities and expectations for professional submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Money / contracts / prepublication / publicity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare for financial and legal aspects of publishing—contracts and rights, budgeting, prepublication tasks, and publicity planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query letters / response and rejection
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft concise, targeted query letters; be prepared for rejection and know how to read responses and revise approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-publishing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider self-publishing as an option—learn production, distribution, and marketing requirements if you choose this route.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slush pile
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the reality of unsolicited submissions: many good manuscripts are filtered out—learn to craft submission materials that stand out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing community / classes / conferences
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage with workshops, classes, and conferences for learning, networking, and development; they are part of a writer's professional ecosystem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character complexity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make characters layered with contradictions and inner life; complexity creates realism and dramatic interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character consistency
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep characters' actions, voice, and beliefs consistent unless development/arc justifies change; inconsistency should be motivated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrasting traits (character)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contrasts in traits to make characters memorable and to generate internal conflict and interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character desire / goal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give characters clear desires/goals that drive action and structure scenes; desire fuels conflict and plot progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue of characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make dialogue reveal character and advance plot; ensure each character's speech patterns are distinct and authentic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting to know characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scenes, actions, reactions, and small details to let readers learn characters organically rather than through exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand roles (protagonist, antagonist, supporting) and archetypes but avoid flat stereotypes—make each character serve story needs while feeling real.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of revealing characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reveal through action, dialogue, choices, and detail; prefer showing to telling when introducing character traits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character names
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose names that suit setting and character, are pronounceable, and avoid confusing similarities among major characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character origins
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider background and past events that shape a character's motivations and behavior; reveal origin details as relevant to the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questions about characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask probing questions (what do they want, what would they never do?) to deepen characterization and create consistent choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant details of characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select details that matter to plot or theme; omit irrelevant minutiae that distract from narrative focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting and characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let setting influence and reveal character (how they act in place, what they notice); make setting integral rather than decorative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoughts of characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use interior thoughts to reveal voice and motive but avoid excessive telling; balance thought with action and dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clichés
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid clichéd images, phrases, and situations; strive for fresh, specific details instead of stock language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climax
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build to a meaningful climax where stakes and consequences converge; ensure it resolves the central conflict in a way earned by the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create clear, escalating conflict (internal and/or external) that forces choices and drives plot; avoid easy resolutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show the results of characters' actions; consequences should follow logically and emotionally from prior choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency in POV contract
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain clear rules for point of view (what the POV character knows and experiences); do not slip into omniscience without setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency in voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustain a coherent narrative voice appropriate to story and POV; abrupt voice shifts break reader immersion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing contracts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand essential contract terms (rights, royalties, deadlines) and negotiate or seek counsel when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know basic copyright protections and how they apply to your work; register if needed for legal enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft (general)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Master core elements—plot, character, scene structure, dialogue, description, voice—and practice through revision and reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis (plot)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place pivotal crises at structural moments to challenge protagonists and pivot plot trajectory; crises should escalate stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cutting (revision)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be ruthless in revision: cut unnecessary scenes, words, and repetitions to tighten pace and clarity; preserve what's essential to story and voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description: emotions and thoughts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe feelings and thoughts via sensory detail and behavior rather than abstract labels; avoid telling the reader what to feel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description: sensory detail
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete sensory specifics (sight, sound, smell, touch, taste) to ground scenes and create immersion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description: setting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Render setting with selective, telling details that contribute to mood, character, or plot rather than exhaustive description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description: specificity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer precise, particular details over vague generalities; specificity makes scenes feel real and unique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description: telling details
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose small, emblematic details that reveal larger truths about character, era, or theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description: traps
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid common pitfalls (over-description, irrelevant detail, melodramatic sentiment); keep description purposeful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description: tricks of the trade
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ reliable techniques (concrete detail, active verbs, sensory anchors) while avoiding hackneyed 'tricks' that readers notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word choice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select precise, tonal words appropriate to voice and scene; strong diction can replace adverbs and excess description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deus ex machina (avoid)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid implausible, unearned resolutions; plot solutions should arise from established elements and character choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialect
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dialect carefully—it can add authenticity but can also distract or caricature; render speech patterns selectively and respectfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue: bad examples
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and avoid bad dialogue (expository, on-the-nose, identical character voices); rewrite to serve subtext and character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue: conventions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow basic conventions of punctuation and formatting; use beats, tags, and action to maintain clarity and rhythm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue: indirect
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use indirect dialogue and implication to convey subtext and inner conflict without explicit statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue: reality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for realistic-sounding speech while keeping dialogue economical—real speech is often repetitious; fiction should distill what's meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue: stage directions / beats
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use small physical actions (beats) to break up dialogue, show mood, and indicate speaker without intrusive tags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue: subtext
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let characters mean more than they say—subtext creates tension and depth in conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue: tags
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer 'said' and minimal tags; use tagging sparingly and avoid flashy synonyms that draw attention to the narration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue: when to use
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include dialogue when it reveals character, advances plot, or provides necessary information; cut idle chatter that stalls pace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match diction to character, setting, and narrative voice—word-level choices shape tone and reader perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distance: emotional
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control emotional distance between narrator and characters to affect reader empathy; closer distance yields immediacy, greater distance yields reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distance: time
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage narrative time distance (immediacy vs. summary) to pace scenes and background information effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distance for editing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create distance (time away) from a draft to spot weaknesses in structure, repetition, and pacing during revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect multiple drafts; the first draft discovers the story, later drafts refine structure, voice, and the economy of language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work constructively with editors—understand editorial roles (developmental vs. copy edit) and be open to substantive revision while defending core choices when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotions: description
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Render emotions through behavior, sensory detail, and physicality rather than abstract labels to create authentic feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotions: distance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use narrative distance to shape how emotions are presented—too close may overwhelm, too distant may deaden emotional impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotions: exposition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid expository dumps of feeling; integrate emotion into scene through stakes and reaction rather than telling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extras (story extras / peripheral elements)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of peripheral elements that don't serve plot or theme; extras can clutter narrative if not purposeful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction (general)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the craft fundamentals—character, plot, scene, voice, and revision—as the core of writing quality fiction.
